That is the design working (nothing runs without my yes), and it is also the clearest sign of where the system has to get better.
> 2. **Every measuring stick in the system has been caught being wrong at least once, and each fix became a rule.** A reviewer that objected to almost everything. A check-back that read the to-do notes instead of the work. A test that gave a perfect score by rubber-stamping. A week when Praxis put himself on the list of projects to kill. The interesting part is not that the system measures itself; it is what happened each time the measurement lied.

Praxis helps me manage my work, and keeps my projects on track towards their goals. Sure, he's a cool pulsing orb and mysterious accent, but his dashboard is full of useful information on exactly what is going through the system at any given time, and my orb indicates what praxis is focused on so I can see his decisions in action.
